newsitem.title: USA: U.S. awaits new China offer on WTO bid--Barshefsky.
newsitem.headline: U.S. awaits new China offer on WTO bid--Barshefsky.

text.p: The United States made clear to China in recent high-level meetings that it expects Beijing to offer a better package of economic reforms in its bid to join the World Trade Organization, acting U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky said Tuesday.

Barshefsky, who just returned from a meeting of Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation leaders in the Philippines, said she believes China's top leadership understands that China will be allowed in the WTO only on a commercially acceptable basis and not as a political deal.
"This is very important," she told reporters.

President Clinton and Chinese President Jiang Zemin talked about the WTO during their meeting this weekend ahead of the APEC leaders gathering, Barshefsky said. She said Clinton made clear Washington's desire to see China become a member of the WTO, which oversees global trade rules and settles disputes, but that Beijing's offers have been inadequate.

"We will not work with the offers on the table," Barshefsky said. She said she believes Chinese leaders now understand the U.S. position. China has insisted on joining the global trading body as a developing nation.
But the Unites States has said China's economy is just too big, and allowing China to follow the more lenient rules of a developing nation would distort the global trade balance.
